title: European Court of Human Rights Grand Chamber rules in Georgia v. Russia (II)
body:
On 21 January 2021 the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in Georgia v. Russia (II) (application no. 38263/08). Georgia had applied to the Court on 11 August 2008 and lodged its full application on 6 February 2009.

On jurisdiction, the Court found that Russia had no jurisdiction over events in the active phase of hostilities, from 8 to 12 August 2008, when control was chaotic and contested. Events after the 12 August ceasefire fell under Russian jurisdiction, based on effective control over South Ossetia, Abkhazia and the buffer zone that continued until troops officially withdrew on 10 October 2008, and on the continuing Russian presence and the dependence of the local authorities.

The Court found administrative practices amounting to violations of the Convention. They covered killings, arson and looting in Georgian villages (Articles 2 and 8 and Article 1 of Protocol No. 1) and the ill-treatment of detained civilians, who were held in Tskhinvali (Articles 3 and 5). It found that Georgian prisoners of war were tortured, that ethnic Georgian displaced persons were prevented from returning home, and that Russia failed to investigate effectively and to submit key evidence. It found insufficient evidence on the right to education. The Court deferred just satisfaction for one year. The Georgian Young Lawyers' Association said it represented more than 350 victims.
